title: 〜ものだ
meaning: that's the way it is / one should… / I used to… / how…!
simpleExplanation: 〜ものだ adds a feeling of "that's just how things are" to a sentence. Depending on the form before it, it does four jobs: (1) a general truth (人は失敗するものだ – people do make mistakes), (2) gentle advice about what one should do (年上の人には敬語を使うものだ), (3) a nostalgic memory with the た-form (よく遊んだものだ – we used to play a lot), and (4) strong emotion or admiration (時間がたつのは早いものだ). The common thread is that the speaker is stating something as a natural, shared feeling rather than a personal opinion.
whenUsed: Both spoken and written. The advice use sounds like a parent or teacher, so avoid it toward superiors. The nostalgic 〜たものだ is common in reminiscing conversation and in essays. Negative advice is 〜ものではない ("one shouldn't").
formation: Verb (dictionary form) + ものだ → general truth / should
Verb (た-form) + ものだ → used to (nostalgia)
Verb (ない form) + ものだ / Verb + ものではない → should not
い-adjective + ものだ / な-adjective + な + ものだ → emotion, admiration

rows.label: Dictionary form + ものだ
cells: 人は誰でも失敗するものだ
Everyone makes mistakes; that's how people are.

rows.label: Dictionary form + ものだ (advice)
cells: Promises are meant to be kept.

rows.label: た-form + ものだ
cells: 子どものころ、よく川で泳いだものだ
As a child I used to swim in the river all the time.

rows.label: Adjective + ものだ
cells: 月日がたつのは早いものだ

examples.ja: 人はだれでも年を取るものだ。
examples.reading: ひとはだれでもとしをとるものだ。
examples.en: Everyone gets old; that's just the way it is.

examples.ja: 目上の人には敬語を使うものだよ。
examples.reading: めうえのひとにはけいごをつかうものだよ。
examples.en: You should use polite language with your seniors, you know.

examples.ja: 学生のころは、朝まで友達と語り合ったものだ。
examples.reading: がくせいのころは、あさまでともだちとかたりあったものだ。
examples.en: In my student days, I used to talk with friends until morning.

examples.ja: 人の悪口を言うものではない。
examples.reading: ひとのわるぐちをいうものではない。
examples.en: One shouldn't speak ill of others.
examples.note: ものではない = should not (moral advice).

examples.ja: 赤ちゃんの成長は本当に早いものですね。
examples.reading: あかちゃんのせいちょうはほんとうにはやいものですね。
examples.en: Babies really do grow up fast, don't they.

similarGrammar.difference: "Should" as the speaker's own judgment. ものだ presents the advice as common sense everyone shares.
Direct advice to a specific person ("the thing to do is…"). ものだ is a general truth, not aimed at one person.
Different pattern: gives a reason ("because…"), often as an excuse.

commonMistakes.wrong: 先生、この言葉は覚えるものですよ。(to a teacher)
commonMistakes.right: 先生、この言葉は覚えたほうがいいと思います。
commonMistakes.why: Advice-ものだ sounds like lecturing. Never use it toward a superior.

commonMistakes.wrong: 昨日、友達と映画を見たものだ。
commonMistakes.right: 昨日、友達と映画を見た。
commonMistakes.why: たものだ is for habitual past ("used to"), not a single event yesterday.

commonMistakes.wrong: 約束は守るものだから、行った。(intending: because I had to keep my promise)
commonMistakes.right: 約束は守るべきだから、行った。／約束したものだから、行った。
commonMistakes.why: ものだから is a separate reason pattern; do not mix it with the truth/advice meaning of ものだ.

usageNotes: Nostalgic たものだ is usually paired with よく, 昔, 子どものころ, 学生時代.
Emotion-ものだ often appears with 本当に, なんと, ずいぶん and ends with ね/なあ in speech.
The casual contraction もんだ is very frequent in speech: 人生って、そんなもんだよ.
jlptTips: In 文法形式の判断, first identify which of the four jobs fits: words like よく + た-form point to "used to"; a moral statement points to "should"; an adjective points to emotion.
Common distractors: ことだ (direct advice), べきだ, ものではない, わけだ. If the sentence is a general truth about people or the world, choose ものだ.
Do not confuse with ものの (although), ものなら (if one could), ものだから (because). Check the syllables after もの carefully.
